correctness.rationale: A full row or column plus a maximal nonattacking rook placement is necessary. If the line has at least three cells it forces the clique side of any attempted extension, proving sufficiency; size-two columns and the \(2\)-by-\(2\) square are separately handled via induced 2K2/C4. Counts and overlap are exhaustive. Fourteen small boards and 1,763,152 candidate subsets independently confirm the coefficients; the proof handles all parameters.

evidence: Cao establishes polynomial-delay enumeration of all maximal induced split subgraphs for arbitrary input graphs.
Brosse thesis Theorem 3.13 proves that every maximal induced split subgraph can be obtained from a maximal clique of the host plus a maximal independent set in the remainder.
broader_coverage.reasoning: This broader prerequisite explains the first structural reduction, but does not give necessary-and-sufficient rook-specific counting without proving that both classes are maximal, identifying the small double-counting boundary, and deriving exact size probabilities. The general enumeration algorithm is not presented as novel.

originality.rationale: The exact labeled rook-board census, its special small-square overlap, its two-point cardinality spectrum and the square-root asymptotic probability law were not found in the inspected published primary texts. The general clique-plus-stable-set reduction is expressly prior art and is not claimed. Residual risk remains for a separate unindexed family-specific enumeration.
residual_risks: General thesis Theorem 3.13 is strong prior coverage of the structural reduction; the specialization is elementary after it.
An unindexed family-specific split vertex-deletion enumeration or OEIS table could already give the exact coefficients.
A source with equivalent lattice-graph/line-graph language may exist beyond inspected full texts.

value.rationale: The natural problem of inclusion-minimal split vertex deletion receives an exact all-solution cardinality distribution on an infinite connected vertex-transitive graph family. The unbounded internal gaps and exact square-root probability crossover expose behavior of typical versus largest maximal solutions beyond scalar extremal values. The result does not rest only on a correct program or an arbitrary small example.
